A data-reporting scenario with any set of quantiles

Source: R/weights.R
reporting_scenario.Rd

The named scenarios "S1" to "S5" cover a five-number summary, its parts, and the 10th and 90th percentiles added to it. A study may report other quantiles, for example the 5th and 95th percentiles, the tertiles, or the median with one extreme. reporting_scenario() describes such a report by the probabilities of its quantiles and by whether the minimum and the maximum are reported. Its result is passed as the argument scenario of se_imputed, c_mu, c_sigma, inflation_factors, estimator_weights and imputed_moments, which then compute the BLUE of the mean and of the SD from these reported values and its exact factors, at any sample size that is at least the number of reported values.

Usage

reporting_scenario(probs = numeric(0), min = FALSE, max = FALSE)

# S3 method for class 'reporting_scenario'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

probs

The probabilities of the reported sample quantiles, strictly between 0 and 1 and strictly increasing, for example c(0.05, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.95). May be empty when only the minimum and the maximum are reported.

min, max

TRUE when the minimum, or the maximum, of the sample is reported.

x

An object returned by reporting_scenario().

...

Not used.

Value

An object of class "reporting_scenario": a list with probs, min, max and labels, the names of the reported values in increasing order (min, then p5, p25, ... for the quantiles, then max). The weights that estimator_weights returns carry these names, and se_imputed takes the reported values in this order.

Details

At least two values must be reported, because the mean and the SD are two unknowns. The reported values need not be symmetric about the median. Only the BLUE is defined for such a scenario: the estimators of Wan, Luo and Shi exist for S1, S2 and S3.

The named scenarios are special cases: "S2" gives the same weights and factors as reporting_scenario(c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75)), and "S5" the same as reporting_scenario(c(0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.9), min = TRUE, max = TRUE).

How a study turned its sample into the reported quantiles is the argument type of the functions that take the scenario: one of the nine definitions of quantile or a rule supplied as a function (see imputed_moments).

Assumptions: an i.i.d. normal sample, as everywhere in the package.

References

Wu Z, Shi J, Tong T (2026). Precision of the imputed mean and standard deviation from the five-number summary. Manuscript.

See also

se_imputed, imputed_moments

Examples

# a study reports the median with the 5th and 95th percentiles, n = 60
sc <- reporting_scenario(c(0.05, 0.5, 0.95))
sc
#> Reporting scenario with 3 reported values: p5, p50, p95
#> Quantiles at the probabilities 0.05, 0.50, 0.95
inflation_factors(60, sc)                       # the exact inflation factors of the BLUE
#>    kappa_mu kappa_sigma 
#>    1.089587    1.212702 
se_imputed(c(2.1, 5.0, 8.4), n = 60, scenario = sc)
#> Imputed mean and SD under the reported values (p5, p50, p95), n = 60, the BLUE, quantile type 7
#>    mu_hat sigma_hat  se_naive     se_mu  se_sigma 
#>    5.0961    2.0124    0.2598    0.2831    0.2242 
#> Factors: C_mu(n) = 0.1407, C_sigma(n) = 0.1114. The weights are $w_mean and $w_sd; every field with str() or unclass().

# the 10th and 90th percentiles with the quartiles: the named scenario S4
s4 <- reporting_scenario(c(0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.9))
all.equal(c_mu(41, s4), c_mu(41, "S4"))
#> [1] TRUE

# the minimum, the median and the third quartile only
c_sigma(30, reporting_scenario(c(0.5, 0.75), min = TRUE))
#> [1] 0.186472
